title: Structure of mathematical proof
statement: Understand and use the structure of mathematical proof, proceeding from given assumptions through a series of logical steps to a conclusion; use methods of proof stated below:

title: Proof by exhaustion
statement: Proof by exhaustion
guidance: Proof by exhaustion. This involves trying all the options. Suppose $x$ and $y$ are odd integers less than 7. Prove that their sum is divisible by 2.

title: Disproof by counterexample
statement: Disproof by counter example.
guidance: Disproof by counter example – show that the statement “$n^2-n+1$ is a prime number for all values of $n$” is untrue.

title: Factor and remainder theorems
statement: Simple algebraic division; use of the Factor Theorem and the Remainder Theorem.
guidance: Only division by $(ax+b)$ or $(ax-b)$ will be required, e.g. students should know that if $f(x)=0$ when $x=\dfrac{b}{a}$, then $(ax-b)$ is a factor of $f(x)$. Students may be required to factorise cubic expressions such as $x^3+3x^2-4$ and $6x^3+11x^2-x-6$. Students should be familiar with the terms 'quotient' and 'remainder' and be able to determine the remainder when the polynomial $f(x)$ is divided by $(ax+b)$.

title: Equation and properties of a circle
statement: Coordinate geometry of the circle using the equation of a circle in the form $(x-a)^2+(y-b)^2=r^2$ and including use of the following circle properties: (i) the angle in a semicircle is a right angle; (ii) the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord; (iii) the perpendicularity of radius and tangent.
guidance: Students should be able to find the radius and the coordinates of the centre of the circle, given the equation of the circle and vice versa.

title: Sequences and recurrence relations
statement: Sequences, including those given by a formula for the $n$th term and those generated by a simple relation of the form $x_{n+1}=f(x_n)$.

title: Arithmetic sequences and series
statement: Understand and work with arithmetic sequences and series, including the formula for the nth term and the sum of a finite arithmetic series; the sum of the first n natural numbers.
guidance: The proof of the sum formula should be known. Understanding of $\Sigma$ notation will be expected.

title: Increasing, decreasing and periodic sequences
statement: Increasing sequences, decreasing sequences and periodic sequences.

title: Geometric sequences and series
statement: Understand and work with geometric sequences and series, including the formulae for the $n$th term and the sum of a finite geometric series; the sum to infinity of a convergent geometric series, including the use of $|r|<1$. Binomial expansion of $(a+bx)^n$ for
guidance: For example, given the sum of a series students should be able to use logarithms to find the value of $n$. The proof of the sum formula for a finite series should be known. The sum to infinity may be expressed as $S_\infty$.

title: Binomial expansion for positive integer n
statement: positive integer $n$.
guidance: The notations $n!$, $\dbinom{n}{r}$ and ${}^nC_r$ may be used.

title: Exponential function y = a^x
statement: $y=a^x$ and its graph.

title: Laws of logarithms
statement: Laws of logarithms.
guidance: To include $\log_a(xy) \equiv \log_a x + \log_a y$, $\log_a\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) \equiv \log_a x - \log_a y$, $\log_a(x^k) \equiv k\log_a x$, $\log_a\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) \equiv -\log_a x$, $\log_a a = 1$, where $a,x,y>0$, $a \neq 1$.

title: Solving a^x = b
statement: The solution of equations of the form $a^x=b$.
guidance: Students may use the change of base formula.

title: Trigonometric identities tan and Pythagorean
statement: Knowledge and use of $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$ and $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$.

title: Solving trigonometric equations
statement: Solution of simple trigonometric equations in a given interval.
guidance: Students should be able to solve equations such as $\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)=\dfrac{3}{4}$ for $0<x<2\pi$, $\cos(x+30^{\circ})=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $-180^{\circ}<x<180^{\circ}$, $\tan 2x=1$ for $90^{\circ}<x<270^{\circ}$, $6\cos^2 x+\sin x-5=0$ for $0 \leq x<360^{\circ}$, $\sin\left(2x+\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)=\dfrac{1}{2}$ for $-\pi \leq x<\pi$.

title: Maxima, minima and stationary points
statement: Applications of differentiation to maxima and minima and stationary points, increasing and decreasing functions.
guidance: To include applications to curve sketching. Maxima and minima problems may be set in the context of a practical problem.

title: Evaluating definite integrals
statement: Evaluation of definite integrals.

title: Area under a curve
statement: Interpretation of the definite integral as the area under a curve.
guidance: Students will be expected to evaluate the area of a region bounded by a curve and given straight lines. For example, find the finite area bounded by the curve $y=6x-x^2$ and the line $y=2x$. $\int x \, dy$ will not be required. Students will be expected to be able to evaluate the area of a region bounded by two curves.

title: Trapezium rule
statement: Approximation of area under a curve using the trapezium rule.
guidance: For example, use the trapezium rule to approximate $\displaystyle\int_0^1 \sqrt{2x+1}\,dx$ using four strips. Use of an increasing number of trapezia to improve accuracy, and an estimate of the error, may be required.

title: Simplifying rational expressions
statement: Simplification of rational expressions including factorising and cancelling, and algebraic division.
guidance: Denominators of rational expressions will be linear or quadratic, e.g. $\dfrac{1}{ax+b}$, $\dfrac{x^3+1}{px^2+qx+r}$, $\dfrac{x-1}{x^2}$.

title: Functions, domain, range and inverses
statement: Definition of a function. Domain and range of functions. Composition of functions. Inverse functions and their graphs.
guidance: The concept of a function as a one-one or many-one mapping from $\mathbb{R}$ (or a subset of $\mathbb{R}$) to $\mathbb{R}$ will be used. The notation $f:x \mapsto f(x)$ may be used. Students should know that $fg$ means 'do $g$ first, then $f$'. Students should know that if $f^{-1}$ exists, then $f^{-1}f(x) = ff^{-1}(x) = x$.

title: The modulus function
statement: The modulus function.
guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graphs of $y=|ax+b|$ and the graphs of $y=|f(x)|$ and $y=f(|x|)$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$. For example, sketch the graph with equation $y=|2x-1|$ and use the graph to solve the equation $|2x-1|=x+5$ or the inequality $|2x-1|>x+5$.

title: Combined graph transformations
statement: Combinations of the transformations $y=f(x)$ as represented by $y=af(x)$, $y=f(x)+a$, $y=f(x+a)$, $y=f(ax)$.
guidance: Students should be able to sketch the graph of, for example, $y=2f(3x)$, $y=f(-x)+1$, given the graph of $y=f(x)$, or the graph of, for example, $y=3+\sin 2x$, $y=-\cos\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$. The graph of $y=f(ax+b)$ will not be required.

title: Reciprocal and inverse trig functions
statement: Knowledge of secant, cosecant and cotangent and of arcsin, arccos and arctan. Their relationships to sine, cosine and tangent. Understanding of their graphs and appropriate restricted domains.
guidance: Angles measured in both degrees and radians.

title: Sec² and cosec² identities
statement: Knowledge and use of $\sec^2\theta = 1+\tan^2\theta$ and $\csc^2\theta = 1+\cot^2\theta$.

title: Compound and double angle formulae
statement: Knowledge and use of double angle formulae; use of formulae for $\sin(A \pm B)$, $\cos(A \pm B)$ and $\tan(A \pm B)$ and of expressions for $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta$ in the equivalent forms of $r\cos(\theta \pm \alpha)$ or $r\sin(\theta \pm \alpha)$.
guidance: To include application to half angles. Knowledge of the $t=\tan\frac{1}{2}\theta$ formulae will not be required. Students should be able to solve equations such as $a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta=c$ in a given interval, and to prove identities such as $\cos x\cos 2x+\sin x\sin 2x \equiv \cos x$.

title: The exponential function e^x
statement: The function $e^x$ and its graph.
guidance: To include the graph of $y=e^{ax+b}+c$. Solution of equations of the form $e^{ax+b}=p$ and

title: The natural logarithm ln x
statement: The function $\ln x$ and its graph; $\ln x$ as the inverse function of $e^x$.
guidance: $\ln(ax+b)=q$ is expected.

title: Using logarithmic graphs to fit models
statement: Use logarithmic graphs to estimate parameters in relationships of the form $y=ax^n$ and $y=kb^x$.
guidance: Plot $\log y$ against $\log x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log a$ and the gradient is $n$. Plot $\log y$ against $x$ and obtain a straight line where the intercept is $\log k$ and the gradient is $\log b$.
